newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures finish down in edgy trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures finish down in edgy trade.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures finished lower in edgy trading before key U.S. data on Friday.

June Standard and Poor's 500 futures sold off late after hitting a fresh session high at 769.50 after a firm Treasury bond futures close. Traders said several firms were good buyers after the bond close.
But the market faltered at the new high and turned on a dime, shaving gains amid good volume, traders said.
June S&P 500s dropped through former support at 763.60, Tuesday's and Wednesday's session low, triggering sell stops that took June to the lowest price all week at 761.50.

"We had a late rally and a late selloff," one S&P 500 futures trader said. "It was mass chaos, good volume," he added. The rally and selloff came against a backdrop of quiet positioning and mild nervousness before Friday's data, he said.

March producer prices and retail sales will be released at 0730 CDT/1230 GMT, giving data-hungry traders the latest glimpse of the U.S. economy. The lineup of economic data has been slim so far this week, and the uptick in the latest weekly jobless claims reported before the open this morning had no impact on the market.
PPI is expected to remain unchanged, with a 0.1-percent rise in the core inflation rate. Retail sales are seen rising 0.6 percent and gaining 0.4 percent without autos.
An S&P 500 futures trader said he was inundated with paper orders in the last hour of trade and said heavy selling reigned, exacerbated by intraday technicals.

Early in the session, June Standard and Poor's 500 futures briefly dipped through key 763.60 support, but initially lacked followthrough and bounced. Several traders had said a move through 763.60 could see losses to 761.50, which turned out to be the level that held losses late.

At the close, June S&P 500s were off 2.25 points to 763.35, Midcap 400s lost 2.20 to 256.05, Russell 2000 lost 1.60 to 348.15, Value Line dropped 1.80 to 692.65, NYSE Composite fell 0.90 to 401.35, Nasdaq 100 dropped 12.85 to 823.90, and Nikkei 225 fell 340.0 to 17,490.0.
